```{r, include=FALSE}
devtools::load_all()
```

`grcg7br` is a personal R package to annotate and visualize genes of chicken genome
[bGalGal1.mat.broiler.GRCg7b](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_016699485.2/).


## Installation

You can use `devtools`:

```r
install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("ymat2/grcg7br")
```

Alternatively, you can use `pak`:

```r
install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("ymat2/grcg7br")
```


## Usage

grcg7br provides 2 functions: `annotate()` and `gggenes()`.

### `annotate()`

This function takes a data frame containing
chromosome, start, and end columns---such as output files from VCFtools---and
annotates genes from GRCg7b assembly that overlap those regions.
Internally, it uses [GenomicRanges](https://github.com/Bioconductor/GenomicRanges).

Example:

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
fst = readr::read_tsv("inst/extdata/sample.fst")
knitr::kable(fst)
```

```{r, message=FALSE}
fst_genes = fst |> grcg7br::annotate(seqname = "CHROM", start = "BIN_START", end = "BIN_END")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::kable(fst_genes)
```

### `gggenes()`

This function visualizes gene structures within a specific genomic range using `ggplot2` ecosystem.

Example:

```{r}
grcg7br::gggenes(
  chrom = "NC_052535.1",
  from = 85000001,
  to = 85150001,
  color = "#A4A082",
  nrow = 3
)
```

You can use a vecter of gene names to show a part of genes in the region:

```{r}
grcg7br::gggenes(
  chrom = "NC_052535.1",
  from = 85000001,
  to = 85150001,
  color = "#A4A082",
  nrow = 3,
  label = c("REEP1", "KDM3A")
)
```

### Other utilities

- `accession2chrom`:
  Cross-reference table between chromosome accession and chromosome number
  (e.g. NC_052532.1 = 1)

- `cumsum_seq_length`:
  Helper dataframe to convert position in chromosome to cumsum position
  (used for manhattan plot)

- `chrom_axis`:
  axis labels and positions for manhattan plot
